This piece of functional art is here to remind you that no matter how gloopy and messy life gets, there is always love and joy bursting through. 🌈💗 I am so excited to finally start sharing the first pieces from my 2026 collection! The first half of this year has been full of learning, experimenting, and pushing my work in new directions. It has also been one of the heaviest seasons of my life. While making this collection, I found myself returning again and again to the same idea: choosing hope. This piece feels like a little celebration of that. A reminder that even when things feel overwhelming, beautiful things can still emerge from the mess. Thankfully, the scary chapter my chosen family has been living through is coming to a very happy ending, and I am sitting in deep gratitude for that. Not everyone gets that outcome, and I don’t take it for granted for a second. So tell me, what makes you stay hopeful when life feels extra gloopy? #ceramicartist #dopaminedecor #glitterinlay #rainbowart #processvideo

This is a process video of how I create my composite filigree pieces. Like this one, I usually use porcelain as my clay body. Combining two separate pieces allows me to work on a larger scale because it would be extremely difficult for me to throw this as a single piece on the wheel. In my YouTube video this weekend I’m recreating some pots I haven’t thrown since 2014, specially store jars with inset, internal galleries and thin lids with thrown knobs. You can find a link to the fully narrated video via the Linktree in my profile’s biography.   I’ve lied a little bit. I did create jars that were similar to this during my apprenticeship with Lisa Hammond between 2014-2017, yet they were bellied pieces with a gallery closer to the jars I make these days, yet they unusual thrown knobs that were in themselves similar to small bowls.   To create pots with internal galleries like this you need to split the rim. One section becomes the lip, the other is coaxed inside and carefully set horizontal to essentially become a ledge onto which the lid can be held aloft. This alone is a tricky task and it involves throwing a form with enough material in the lip to withstand such a manoeuvre. Secondly, there’s the small disc-like lid, a form that’s thrown off-the-hump and then the following day it’s trimmed back to have its more exacting shape and the knob is thrown on, again, a tricky task as it involves fiddly, fingertip throwing and a lot of accuracy.   All of this and more will be covered in my longer, narrated YouTube upload. I enjoyed making these and since it has been such a long time since I’ve crafted them, my skillset in the interim has improved massively, thus I could apply newly learnt techniques and ability into making shapes I used to struggle with to some degree. I hope you like the film if you happen to click over and watch it, it’s greatly appreciated if you do as it helps to keep the lights on in the workshop.   #pottery #ceramics #handmade #jar #satisfying
